subject: Finovate — model fit evals & benchmark links
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie.park@finovate.com>
Cc:  
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Finovate discovery — next steps & proposed evals

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Finovate's use case for interactive financial assistant workflows. Quick recap and proposed next steps:  

- Goal: real-time account lookup + personalized guidance for support agents (strict PII controls).
- Key constraints: <= 150ms P50 latency for short completions, sensible cost per 1k QPS, and strong safety/QA on hallucination reduction for account-sensitive prompts.

Proposed next steps:
1) You send over a ~200-row sample of anonymized prompts (schema looks good) — Sophie said you could share this by EOD Tue.
2) We'll run a model-fit eval across 3 candidate model configs and share Redwood-verified benchmark links (TPS, latency percentiles, token cost) + prompt set.
3) Quick follow-up demo with results and recommended rollout plan (30 min) — propose Thu 10am PT.

Initial candidates I recommend for the eval (based on today's workload):
- redwood-13b-ptq (good latency/cost tradeoff for short responses)
- redwood-70b-q4 (higher quality, higher cost — useful for complex multi-step reasoning)
- redwood-13b-ptq + prefix caching (if your traffic reuses prefixes heavily it can cut token cost ~30%)

I will include Alex (model ops) and Marissa (customer success) on the follow-up so we can surface SLA/rollout guidance.

Benchmark artifacts we will produce:
- Redwood-verified performance profile per model (TPS, P50/P90/P95 latency, memory usage)
- Prompt set used for evaluation, and a short eval harness with expected pass/fail criteria (quality regression checks)
- CSV of per-sample outputs and scoring so you can review edge cases

I’ll kick off the eval as soon as we receive the sample.

Thanks — talk soon,

Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Schedule: https://cal.com/jordan-blake/30

From: Sophie Park <sophie.park@finovate.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finovate Research <research@finovate.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Finovate discovery — next steps & proposed evals

Jordan —

Thanks for the recap and clear plan. Attached is a zipped sample export (anonymized) — contains ~230 prompt/intent rows and a short mapping file. Our priorities are latency (we need consistent sub-200ms for interactive snippets) and avoiding hallucinations on account data. Cost is a secondary consideration but important for scaling.

Can you confirm whether the 13b-ptq variant supports our privacy controls (KMS + customer-keyed encryption) when run in Redwood Dedicated? Also happy to do Thu 10am PT — works for our team.

Best,

Sophie Park
Director, Product — Finovate

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie.park@finovate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Finovate discovery — next steps & proposed evals

Thanks Sophie — received the sample, appreciate the fast turnaround. Quick answers and what we'll deliver ahead of Thu:

1) Privacy/KMS: yes — redwood-13b-ptq and all Dedicated variants can be configured with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). I'll have our security pack ready for you (SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration notes) by tomorrow.

2) Running the evals: we started a lightweight run this morning (see attached artifacts). Summary results (preliminary):
- redwood-13b-ptq: 450 TPS in our standard 8-GPU pool; latency P50=82ms, P90=165ms, P95=210ms (short completions profile).
- redwood-70b-q4: 120 TPS; latency P50=210ms, P90=340ms, P95=410ms.
- redwood-13b-ptq + prefix cache: effective token cost reduced ~28% on this sample; latency P50 ~90ms (cache warm).

Note: TPS measured under our continuous batching harness (mixed short and medium sequences). We always publish both batch-level TPS and per-request latency percentiles — links below point to the Redwood-verified performance profiles where these numbers and fuller run logs are available.

3) Quality / regression concerns:
- We’ll run a focused quality regression suite against your labeled cases and a small adversarial prompt set (to look for hallucinations around account identifiers).
- If we see regression vs your baseline thresholds we recommend either (a) moving to the 70b variant for the failing prompts, or (b) adding a small retrieval step + reranker (we can demo both).

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_finovate_jul2026.csv (per-sample latencies + scores), prompt_set_finovate_v1.json (the exact prompts used).

Shared links:  
- Performance profiles: https://app.redwood.ai/profiles/verified/redwood-13b-ptq (includes TPS and percentile charts)
- 70b profile: https://app.redwood.ai/profiles/verified/redwood-70b-q4
- Drive folder with CSVs and outputs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwood-Finovate-Benchmarks

Next steps:
- Thu 10am PT demo (confirm RSVP) — we will present the evaluation dashboard, per-sample failure cases, and recommended rollout plan (canary + auto-fallback).
- If you want, Alex can scope a Dedicated capacity estimate for production throughput based on the TPS numbers.

Would you like us to prioritize reducing P95 for the 13b-ptq run (we can tune batching and kernel selection) or focus on quality regressions first?

Thanks,

Jordan
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal — Finovate follow-up / MAP & security pack

Jordan / Alex —

Good notes in the thread — a couple of quick internal asks before the Thu demo:  

1) Jordan: please prepare a 1-page mutual action plan (MAP) for Finovate that includes milestones for eval completion, security review (SOC2/KMS), Dedicated sizing, and a proposed pilot timeline (30–60 days). Put estimated costs for both 13b-ptq and 70b-q4.

2) Alex: can you prepare a Dedicated capacity ballpark and include the autoscaling/burst options. Use the TPS numbers Jordan reported as a baseline; include expected token/unit costs per 1k QPS.

3) Add a short section in the deck describing our quality regression checks (prompt-level scoring thresholds + rollback policy). Finovate is explicitly worried about hallucinations on account-specific fields, so show how we surface failing cases and recommended mitigations (retrieval + rerank / 70b for edge cases).

I'll own the security pack compile (SOC2 + KMS notes) and send to Sophie prior to the demo.

Thanks — will join Thu's demo.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
